writeup.p: Spawns a particle burst at a world position with random offset, speed, and count. The particle name is a String that the client maps to an EnumParticleTypes; a trailing varint array carries iconcrack/blockcrack item and block data. Server-side it is the workhorse of WorldServer.spawnParticle, which batches particles into a single packet and sends it with a long-distance flag when the emitter is far from the viewer. The client handler walks the count in a loop, so a large count is a direct CPU/GPU cost on the receiving machine.

NetHandlerPlayClient.handleParticles marshals to the main thread, then calls clientWorldController.spawnParticle. When count is 0 the offset floats are treated as a single particle's velocity; otherwise the offsets are random spread and count particles are spawned. A Throwable around the spawn call logs 'Could not spawn particle effect' instead of crashing. The server path (WorldServer.spawnParticle) constructs one S2A per batch and uses sendToAllNear with a 512-block radius when longDistance is set.

Five distinct uses in the 8 clients. (1) Memeware 7.3 Disabler cancels every S2A unconditionally, an anti-lag/anti-crash blanket filter. (2) Rise 5.99 Disabler cancels only SLIME-type particles in its HypixelSlime mode. (3) Rise 6.x ParticleDistanceComponent, a performance component, drops any particle further than 6 blocks from the player. (4) Rise 6.x ParticleCheck, a security feature, token-buckets particle counts and drops floods. (5) Tenacity 6.0 AntiExploit cancels particles with extreme speed or count, and Sigma 4.11 Criticals skips S2A inside its own packet state machine so the crit-trigger logic is not disturbed.

Particle floods are a classic client-crash vector: a server sends one S2A with a huge count or repeated packets, and the client spawns thousands of entities per tick. Anti-cheat servers also use particle bursts as visual flags for cheaters (crit particles on KillAura, etc.). Client defenses range from blanket cancellation (Memeware) to rate limiting (Rise ParticleCheck: accumulate count, drain 6 per packet, cap 150, drop over 100) to heuristic drops (Tenacity: speed >= 1 or count > 1). The trade-off is visibility: aggressive cancellation hides legitimate gameplay effects.

overview: The particle broadcast packet, and the only one of the six where client defense depth actually shows: blanket cancel (Memeware), selective cancel (Rise 5.99 slime mode), distance culling (Rise 6.x performance component), flood rate limiting (Rise 6.x ParticleCheck), and crash heuristics (Tenacity AntiExploit). Sigma's Criticals skips it inside its packet state machine.
server_handling: WorldServer.spawnParticle builds one S2APacketParticles per batch with particle type, longDistance flag, x/y/z floats, three offset floats, speed, count, and a varint data array. It sends via ConfigurationManager.sendToAllNear (radius 512 when longDistance, else 32). NetHandlerPlayClient.handleParticles then loops count times through clientWorldController.spawnParticle, which is where a flood becomes a client-side hang. No server-side cap exists on count in vanilla 1.8.9.
protocol_notes: Encoding: String particle name, boolean longDistance, float x, float y, float z, float offsetX, float offsetY, float offsetZ, float speed, int count, then a varint-length int array of particle arguments used only by iconcrack and blockcrack. The name is read with readStringFromBuffer(64). Count 0 is special: offsets become velocity for a single particle. The packet was introduced in 1.8 with the EnumParticleTypes refactor that replaced the older string-only effect packets.
anticheat_landscape: Anti-cheats use particles as a side channel rather than flagging the packet itself: critical-hit particles around a target are evidence for killaura checks on servers that render them. The client-side countermeasures here are defensive, not evasive. The interesting tension is Rise ParticleCheck's accumulator: it treats particle arrival as a budget (drain 6 per packet, cap 150, drop when the bucket exceeds 100), which keeps normal combat particles while killing flood attempts. Blanket cancels (Memeware) trade all particle feedback for stability.

modules.name: Disabler (particle cancel)
modules.purpose: Remove particle traffic client-side: blanket in Memeware, selective slime-only in Rise 5.99.
modules.how_it_works: Memeware's Disabler registers a PacketInEvent consumer that cancels every S2A it sees, unconditionally, regardless of mode. Rise 5.99's Disabler, in HypixelSlime mode, checks the particle type and cancels only EnumParticleTypes.SLIME. Nekoware's Disabler imports the class but ships no active particle handler in the file.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Invisible server-side: cancelled clientbound packets are never acknowledged. The cost is losing all particle feedback, which some servers use as hit indicators.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 restricts the cancel to SLIME particles in the HypixelSlime mode. Nekoware v1 private imports S2APacketParticles in its Disabler but has no handler using it (dead import).

modules.name: ParticleDistanceComponent (performance)
modules.purpose: Drop particle packets whose origin is more than 6 blocks away to save GPU work.
modules.how_it_works: A Component (non-module system) listening on PacketReceiveEvent. For each S2A it computes the squared distance from the player to the packet origin and cancels the packet when distanceSq >= 36, i.e. 6 blocks. Particles closer than 6 blocks pass through untouched.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: No anti-cheat exposure; it is a pure client-performance filter. Aggressive distance culling can hide distant particle cues like explosions or beacon effects.

modules.name: ParticleCheck (security)
modules.purpose: Rate-limit inbound particle volume so a malicious server cannot crash the client with a flood.
modules.how_it_works: A SecurityFeature. For each S2A it adds the packet's particle count to an accumulator, drains 6 per packet, and clamps the bucket at 150. The packet is dropped when the bucket exceeds 100, or when count is < 1, |count| > 20, or speed is negative or above 1000. Normal combat particles pass because their per-packet counts are small.
modules.vanilla_hook: Security pipeline handle(Packet) on the receive path.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Defends the client against particle-crash exploits. The drain rate and 100-threshold are tuned so that even heavy combat (crit, sweep, potion particles) never trips it.
modules.variations: Identical file in Rise 6.1.30. Tenacity 6.0 AntiExploit implements the same idea with simpler heuristics (see its own entry).

modules.name: AntiExploit (particle flood)
modules.purpose: Cancel particle packets that look like crash attempts while logging the block.
modules.how_it_works: A PacketReceiveEvent handler. For S2A it cancels and prints 'Blocked Exploit: Particles' when |particleSpeed| >= 1, or 'Blocked Exploit: Crash' when particleCount > 1. The module bundles several crash-vector filters (resource pack URLs, camera spectate, explosion strength) with a shared 100-packet-per-second counter.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The heuristic is aggressive enough that servers emitting unusual particle effects (custom enchant glints, heavy weather) get filtered. ChatUtil.print spam on each block is a minor DoS surface by itself.
modules.variations: Rise 6.x uses the token-bucket ParticleCheck instead; Tenacity's version trades precision for simplicity.

modules.name: Criticals (packet skip)
modules.purpose: Keep S2A out of the critical-hit packet state machine so it cannot reset the spoofed-position sequence.
modules.how_it_works: In the EventPacket branch of Criticals, an early return fires when the packet is S2A, so particle broadcasts never reach the transaction/position logic below. The handler's state machine tracks C0F transactions and C03 position packets to trigger criticals; particle noise would otherwise be type-checked pointlessly.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Skipping particles has no anti-cheat effect; it is a micro-optimization and a guard against future code paths that might misinterpret clientbound noise.
modules.variations: No other client in the corpus touches S2A from a combat module.

general_hooks: Every handler sits on the packet receive path: Memeware PacketInEvent, Tenacity and Rise 6.x PacketReceiveEvent, Sigma EventPacket, Rise security chain handle(Packet).
client_variations: Memeware cancels via event.cancel() on a custom bus. Rise 6.x components and security features use event.setCancelled() or pipeline drop. Sigma returns early inside a single handler. Tenacity combines cancel with a per-second packet counter shared across crash vectors.
